text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Sudden spike in 5xx from APAC edge -> routed to EU-backed pool. Metric: global-5xx-rate increased from 0.2% to 6.8% in the last 2m. Autodeploy fallback did not trigger. Investigate. Link: https://telemetry/redwood/alerts/3310004321

alice_m: got paged, looking. can someone grab initial blast radius & customer impact?

oncall-runbook-bot: Runbook: Cross-region routing degradation -> https://playbooks/redwood/cross-region-routing. Steps: 1) collect probe traces 2) check routing-policy-flags 3) optional pin to primary region 4) rollback recent policy changes

ben_sre: I pulled traces, APAC clients show ~40% of flows hitting eu-west1 and 20% 502/504. latency not huge but backend responses are 5xx. suspect misapplied steering policy or stale DNS pins. grabbing `route-policy show --id reap-331` now.

navin_net: I'm on networking. no infra deploys in last 30m. we rolled a traffic-weight change at 3310003000 (earlier) for a/c testing. Could be a policy race. pinging infra-traffic for plan.

katy_prod: customer reports: some API keys seeing high error rates, support queue ticked up. we've got at least one SSO customer with signin failures. Jordan, can you classify severity?

jordan_support: ticket surge: ~12 customers reporting errors, 3 high-priority (auth flows). estimated affected requests ~2.3k/min at peak. marking P1 for those customers.

alice_m: reproduction from my laptop: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/health` returns 502 when routed to eu-west1. When I force-region ap-southeast1 it's 200. So eu-west1 pool is failing for some APAC traffic path.

ben_sre: here's routing-policy diff I fetched:
```
- region_weights: {apac: 0.7, eu: 0.3}
+ region_weights: {apac: 0.35, eu: 0.65}
change_id: traffic-weight-rollout-3310003000
```
That matches Navin's note. Looks like a flip pushed too wide without canary.

navin_net: checking BGP/ASN flap logs and egress paths. no BGP flaps. DNS TTLs were temporarily lowered to 30s during rollout; could have amplified quick refills.

alice_m: can we pin affected customers back to APAC quickly? what's the safe mitigation?

oncall-runbook-bot: Suggested mitigations: `pin-customer-region --customer <id> --region ap-southeast1` or `rollback-policy --change-id traffic-weight-rollout-3310003000`

ben_sre: initiating rollback of the traffic-weight-change now (rolling back weights to previous profile). Running `trafficctl rollback --id traffic-weight-rollout-3310003000 --confirm`. Will watch telemetry.

incident-bot: action logged: rollback started by ben_sre at 3310004390. Notifying routing controllers.

katy_prod: notify customers. I'm drafting a short message to affected customers with status & ETA.

jordan_support: adding note to support tickets: "We're rolling back a recent routing change to restore normal service. We'll update in 10m."

ben_sre: rollback complete according to control plane at 3310004475. Telemetry: global-5xx-rate dropping from 6.8% -> 0.9% over next 60s. APAC->APAC hits rising.

navin_net: confirmed no route leaks, BGP ok. DNS cache churn high but TTLs back to 300s now. will watch for residual misroutes for next 10m as caches drain.

alice_m: running quick sweep: synthetic checks show success. product smoke looks green.

katy_prod: sending customer update: "We've rolled back a recent routing change which restored normal behavior. We're monitoring and will send a postmortem." :white_check_mark:

jordan_support: customers updated. queues stabilizing.

ben_sre: quick root-cause hypothesis: aggressive weight flip + low TTLs caused a large fraction of APAC clients to be shifted to EU pool, where a transient backend failure (separate) amplified errors -> customer impact. We'll separate the backend failure RCA.

navin_net: action items: 1) add automatic canary enforcement to weight flips (limit regional delta) 2) prevent TTL drops during weight experiments 3) carve out emergency pin CLI for rapid per-customer mitigation

alice_m: assigning postmortem owners: ben_sre (routing rollback and telemetry), navin_net (networking policy & TTLs), katy_prod (customer comms). postmortem due EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STABILITY: resolved->monitoring. duration: ~8m (3310004321 -> 3310004800). Incident record: https://incidents.redwood/3310004321

ben_sre: leaving a note: if you see residual 502s, collect `curl -I` and `tracepath` & paste here.

alice_m: handing off monitoring to night-sre in 20m. @ben_sre can you do a quick handoff summary?

ben_sre: handoff: rollback completed, metrics trending to baseline, DNS TTLs restored, recommended watchlist: api-auth errors, global-5xx-rate, apac->eu ratio. paging thresholds lowered to 1.5% for next 2h. ping me if anything flares.

navin_net: I'll followup with a config change PR to require canary windows for weight changes.

katy_prod: thanks all. closing communications loop once postmortem is posted.

jordan_support: closing P1 tickets once customers confirm 24h stability.

incident-bot: Reaction summary: :thumbsup: x8, :tada: x1, :eyes: x3
